presentation.label: VEL HUMANISE
presentation.summary: Per track, every trig's velocity gets a random offset of up to ±N, set with FUNC + VEL on the TRIG page.
presentation.overview: Velocity Humanise gives each track a random velocity offset: every trig's velocity moves by a random amount up to ±N, clamped to 1..127. N is one of sixteen steps from 0 to 64, set by holding FUNC and turning VEL on the TRIG page, where the label reads RND and the knob becomes a sixteen-position selector. N is per pattern track, kept in core-ar2's mod storage and saved with the pattern. It is an elemod port of MrScruff's rytm-mods 0003-velocity-humanise, with his code unchanged apart from the storage port.
highlights: FUNC + VEL sets a per-track random velocity range.
Sixteen steps from 0 to 64; 0 is stock behaviour.
Kept in core-ar2 mod storage and saved with the pattern.
No longer needs Euclid Accents in the same build.
usage: Use a build containing Velocity Humanise. On the TRIG page, hold FUNC and turn VEL: the label reads RND and the popup shows N.
Set N to 32 and play a track of equal-velocity trigs: the hits vary in level. Set N to 0: they are equal again.
Release FUNC: VEL is the trig velocity again, unchanged.

access.location: TRIG page: the VEL knob with FUNC held.
steps: Hold FUNC and turn VEL to set N.

controls.name: FUNC + VEL (TRIG page)
controls.doc: Sets the track's random velocity range N: sixteen steps from 0 to 64. Each trig's velocity moves by a random amount up to ±N, clamped to 1..127.

limitations: Built for OS 1.74 only. 1.2.0 reaches its parameter through core-ar2's parameter table (core_params, core-ar2 0.4 and later; Modwerk's base is core-ar2 0.7). 1.1.0 detoured the entries of param_apply_delta and param_value_text itself, which core-ar2 0.4 and later own, so it does not link with them.
Needs core-ar2's mod storage: four bits per pattern track (vel_rnd).
On stock firmware, or a build without this module, the track plays its plain velocities: N is in mod storage, which stock ignores.

Not beside Sample RATE: both patch the start of param_short_name (0x400a9000), the knob label routine, for different parameters (VEL here, FIN there). Modwerk's base (core-ar2 0.7) has no shared hook for labels; core-ar2 0.10's knob-name service would let them share.

load.display: Small: a storage read, a random draw and a clamp on each trig
load.conditions: Static: one detour runs per trig in the sequencer; it reads the track's N through core_store_get, which masks interrupts briefly, then draws and clamps the offset. The others run on UI edits and drawing. Not a measurement.

hardware.summary: Iced-Cream reports that on an Analog Rytm MKII with OS 1.74, velocity-humanise 1.2 (this source; rytm2_mods core-pages 7ff47d7, released unchanged in v1.3) passed in P4A4, core-ar2 0.4 with all eleven rytm2_mods ports (2026-10-21): FUNC + VEL on the TRIG page read RND and stepped 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, VEL without FUNC turned the real velocity as on stock, and the RND amount was kept through a power-cycle without SAVE PROJECT. U4A4, core-ar2 0.4's final version with the same eleven objects (the bytes of rytm2_mods v1.3), passed the core's page-key steps the same day. The playback checks of the random velocity spread 1.1 passed were not repeated on 1.2: 1.2 changes only how its parameter's turn and text are reached.
limitations: P4A4: .syx 1c0311697543789316c10dbbbfa78b9a717a180eb26611f2f0d1b732a428d65c. U4A4: .syx 18681f8709242b9d3c5117335a81cd5659ea01c583e3e8477d536e379517b785. Firmware was not read back from the device.
Both builds use core-ar2 0.4, not Modwerk's base (core-ar2 0.7); this package has not been flashed on its own.
The playback checks of the random velocity spread 1.1 passed were not repeated on 1.2.

tests.summary: Hardware: velocity-humanise 1.2 on an Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74, with core-ar2 0.4 and the other rytm2_mods ports (P4A4, 2026-10-21): FUNC + VEL reads RND and steps through N's sixteen values, VEL alone is stock, and N survives a power-cycle without a project save. Modwerk's package linked with core-ar2 0.7 gives a main OS byte-identical to the rytm2_mods v1.3 release object linked with it. In the emulator on the Modwerk base (VH12), FUNC relabels VEL as RND and turning it shows N.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Use a build containing Velocity Humanise. On the TRIG page, hold FUNC and turn VEL: the label reads RND and the popup shows N.
Set N to 32 and play a track of equal-velocity trigs: the hits vary in level. Set N to 0: they are equal again.
Release FUNC: VEL is the trig velocity again, unchanged.
